body.p: Berkley Arms hotel was a hotel.

div.head: In the directories
div.p: The Berkley Arms is in the directories from 1872 to 1905, in Berkley Street just north of Queensberry Street, between Trinity Cottages (later Caroline Cottages) and the Queensberry Street corner. It has no street number; its neighbours are Nos 95 and 101. It is spelt "Berkeley Arms" up to 1878 and in 1885, and "Berkley Arms" in the other years. See Hotels.

The directories list the proprietors as E. O'Hare (1872 to 1873), Philip Davis (1874), M. A. Pearce (1875), William Lyons (1876), Daniel Carroll (1877 to 1880), William R. Hull (1885), Patrick Barry (1890), Joseph Alberd (1895), Wm. Lissaman (1900) and Miss M. White (1905).

div.head: Neighbours
div.p: Swan and Co., engineers and millwrights, are near it in 1880, Cochrane & Scott, ironfounders, in 1890, and the Commonwealth Coach Factory and the Art Furniture Co. in 1905.
